title: Ik ben Sanne
subtitle: Introducing yourself
intro: After this lesson you can introduce yourself in Dutch: say your name, ask someone else's name, and say where you come from. You will also learn when to use **je** and **u**.

words.note: Polite; use with older strangers and officials.
Used for more than one person.

words.forms: ik ben, jij bent, u bent, hij/zij/het is, wij zijn, jullie zijn, zij zijn
ik heet, jij heet, u heet, hij/zij/het heet, wij heten, jullie heten, zij heten
words.note: Use **heten**, not **zijn**, in the question **Hoe heet je?**.

words.forms: ik kom uit, jij komt uit, u komt uit, hij/zij komt uit, wij/jullie/zij komen uit
words.note: The question is **Waar kom je vandaan?**.
Can mean the group of students or the room.

example.nl: Meneer De Vries is de leraar.
example.en: Mr De Vries is the teacher.

words.note: Title for a woman; use with a surname or alone.

example.nl: Meneer De Vries is de leraar.
example.en: Mr De Vries is the teacher.

words.note: Title for a man; use with a surname or alone.

example.en: Pleased to meet you, I am Sanne.

words.note: A polite way to say 'pleased to meet you'.

phrases.note: Use with older strangers and officials.
Also used to give your name.
The word **vandaan** stays at the end.
Slightly formal; common when you meet someone new.

grammar.title: Subject pronouns: ik, jij, u
grammar.explanation: Dutch verbs change with the subject. Learn these pronouns first. **jij** and **zij** are stressed; **je** and **ze** are common unstressed forms. **u** is the polite form of 'you'.
grammar.tip: Use **u** with older strangers and officials. With classmates, use **je**.

grammar.title: **Zijn**: ik ben, jij bent, hij is
grammar.explanation: **Zijn** means 'to be'. The forms are irregular, so learn them as a block. The polite **u** uses **bent**, just like **jij**.

examples.nl: Meneer De Vries is de leraar.
examples.en: Mr De Vries is the teacher.

grammar.tip: **U bent** is the polite form; **jij bent** is informal.

grammar.title: **Heten**: ik heet, jij heet
grammar.explanation: Use **heten** to give your name. The question **Hoe heet je?** means 'What is your name?'. Do not use **zijn** for the question: **Hoe ben je?** is not used for names. The polite question is **Hoe heet u?**.
grammar.tip: **Ik ben Sanne** is also fine, but the question is **Hoe heet je?**.

dialogue.title: Eerste dag in de klas
dialogue.setting: First day of a Dutch course in Utrecht; two students meet before the teacher arrives.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.nl: Hallo, ik ben Daan. Hoe heet jij?
lines.en: Hi, I am Daan. What is your name?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Hoi Daan, ik heet Sanne. Leuk je te ontmoeten.
lines.en: Hi Daan, my name is Sanne. Nice to meet you.

lines.speaker: Daan
lines.en: Pleased to meet you. Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ik kom uit Nederland. En jij?
lines.en: I come from the Netherlands. And you?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Is meneer De Vries de leraar?
lines.en: Is Mr De Vries the teacher?

lines.speaker: Meneer De Vries
lines.nl: Goedemorgen. Ik ben meneer De Vries.
lines.en: Good morning. I am Mr De Vries.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Goedemorgen, meneer. Ik heet Sanne. Aangenaam.
lines.en: Good morning, sir. My name is Sanne. Pleased to meet you.

lines.speaker: Meneer De Vries
lines.nl: Aangenaam, Sanne. Waar kom je vandaan?
lines.en: Pleased to meet you, Sanne. Where are you from?

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks for someone's name informally?
exercises.explain: **Hoe heet je?** asks for a name; the other sentences ask where someone is from or how they are.

exercises.prompt: You speak to an older official for the first time. Which word for 'you' is best?
exercises.explain: **U** is the polite form; **jij** is for peers and **jullie** means 'you' plural.
Use **komen uit** and put **vandaan** at the end: **Waar kom je vandaan?**
Use **komen uit** for origin: **Ik kom uit Engeland.**

mistakes.pattern: Forgets the subject pronoun ('Heet Sanne.' / 'Ben Sanne.')
mistakes.explain: Start with the subject: 'Ik heet Sanne.' or 'Ik ben Sanne.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses both verbs together ('Ik ben heet Sanne.')
mistakes.explain: Choose one verb: 'Ik heet Sanne' or 'Ik ben Sanne.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'bent' with 'ik' ('Ik bent Sanne.')
mistakes.explain: With **ik** use **ben**: 'Ik ben Sanne.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'heten' with 'ik' ('Ik heten Sanne.')
mistakes.explain: With **ik** the form is **heet**: 'Ik heet Sanne.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'komt' with 'je' ('Waar komt je vandaan?')
mistakes.explain: With **je** use **kom**: 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts **vandaan** before **je** ('Waar kom vandaan je?')
mistakes.explain: **vandaan** goes at the end: 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses formal **u** for the informal prompt ('Waar komt u vandaan?')
mistakes.explain: The prompt is informal, so use **je**: 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Forgets **vandaan** ('Waar kom je?')
mistakes.explain: Add **vandaan** for 'from': 'Waar kom je vandaan?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **bent** with **hij** ('Hij bent de leraar.')
mistakes.explain: With **hij** use **is**: 'Hij is de leraar.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts **de leraar** before **is** ('Hij de leraar is.')
mistakes.explain: The verb **is** comes second: 'Hij is de leraar.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **ben** with **hij** ('Hij ben de leraar.')
mistakes.explain: The form for **hij** is **is**: 'Hij is de leraar.'

exercises.context: You meet a new classmate. She says:

say.nl: Hallo, ik ben Lotte. Hoe heet jij?
say.en: Hi, I'm Lotte. What's your name?

exercises.task: Say hello and give your name.
examples: Hoi Lotte, mijn naam is Alex.

mistakes.pattern: Does not greet Lotte ('Ik heet Alex.')
mistakes.explain: Start with **Hoi** or **Hallo**: 'Hoi Lotte, ik heet Alex.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses both **ben** and **heet** ('Hoi Lotte, ik ben heet Alex.')
mistakes.explain: Choose one: 'Ik ben Alex' or 'Ik heet Alex'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses **bent** with **ik** ('Hoi Lotte, ik bent Alex.')
mistakes.explain: With **ik** use **ben**: 'Ik ben Alex.'

mistakes.pattern: Forgets the verb with **mijn naam** ('Hoi Lotte, mijn naam Alex.')
mistakes.explain: Say 'Mijn naam is Alex' or 'Ik heet Alex.'

examples: Ik kom uit Engeland. En jij?

mistakes.pattern: Uses **ben** for origin ('Ik ben uit Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: Use **kom uit**: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **van** instead of **uit** ('Ik kom van Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: For countries use **uit**: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts **uit Engeland** before the verb ('Ik uit Engeland kom.')
mistakes.explain: The verb comes second: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **komt** with **ik** ('Ik komt uit Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: With **ik** use **kom**: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

roleplay.title: First day in the language class
roleplay.setting: You are new in a Dutch class in Utrecht. You meet a classmate before the lesson.

say.nl: Hallo! Ik ben Daan. Hoe heet jij?
say.en: Hi! I'm Daan. What's your name?

turns.task: Say hello and give your name.
examples: Hoi Daan, mijn naam is Alex.

mistakes.pattern: Does not greet Daan ('Ik ben Alex.')
mistakes.explain: Start with **Hoi** or **Hallo**: 'Hoi Daan, ik ben Alex.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses both **ben** and **heet** ('Ik ben heet Alex.')
mistakes.explain: Choose one: 'Ik ben Alex' or 'Ik heet Alex'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses **bent** with **ik** ('Ik bent Alex.')
mistakes.explain: With **ik** use **ben**: 'Ik ben Alex.'

mistakes.pattern: Forgets the verb with **mijn naam** ('Mijn naam Alex.')
mistakes.explain: Say 'Mijn naam is Alex' or 'Ik heet Alex.'

say.nl: Leuk je te ontmoeten. Waar kom je vandaan?
say.en: Nice to meet you. Where are you from?

mistakes.pattern: Uses **ben** for origin ('Ik ben uit Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: Use **kom uit**: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **van** instead of **uit** ('Ik kom van Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: For countries use **uit**: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

mistakes.pattern: Forgets **uit** ('Ik kom Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: Say 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **komt** with **ik** ('Ik komt uit Engeland.')
mistakes.explain: With **ik** use **kom**: 'Ik kom uit Engeland.'

say.nl: Aangenaam. Ik kom uit Nederland. Hoe gaat het?
say.en: Pleased to meet you. I'm from the Netherlands. How are you?

examples: Prima, dank je. En met jou?

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'Ik ben goed' for 'I am well'.
mistakes.explain: Use 'Goed' or 'Het gaat goed', not 'Ik ben goed'.

mistakes.pattern: Says 'En jou?' instead of 'En jij?' / 'En met jou?'.
mistakes.explain: The subject form is **jij**: 'En jij?' or 'En met jou?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'Ik gaat goed' ('I goes well') instead of 'Het gaat goed'.
mistakes.explain: Do not say 'Ik gaat goed'; say 'Het gaat goed' or just 'Goed'.

say.nl: Goed, dank je. Is meneer De Vries de leraar?
say.en: Good, thanks. Is Mr De Vries the teacher?

turns.task: Say yes, he is the teacher.
examples: Ja, meneer De Vries is de leraar.

mistakes.pattern: Uses **bent** with **hij** ('Ja, hij bent de leraar.')
mistakes.explain: With **hij** use **is**: 'Ja, hij is de leraar.'

mistakes.pattern: Keeps question order ('Ja, is hij de leraar?')
mistakes.explain: Answer with statement order: 'Ja, hij is de leraar.'

mistakes.pattern: Puts **de leraar** before **is** ('Ja, hij de leraar is.')
mistakes.explain: The verb **is** comes second: 'Ja, hij is de leraar.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses **ben** with **hij** ('Ja, hij ben de leraar.')
mistakes.explain: The form for **hij** is **is**.

mistakes.pattern: Uses a morning greeting as goodbye ('Goedemorgen!')
mistakes.explain: Use **Doei** or **Tot ziens** to say goodbye.

mistakes.pattern: Says **Tot morgen** after **Tot straks**.
mistakes.explain: **Tot straks** means later today; reply **Tot straks** or **Doei**.

mistakes.pattern: Says **Welterusten** in the daytime.
mistakes.explain: **Welterusten** is only for bedtime; use **Doei** or **Tot ziens**.

culture.title: Using je and u
culture.text: In the Netherlands, **je/jij** is normal with classmates, colleagues, children and most people you meet socially. Use **u** with older strangers, officials and in formal service situations. Many Dutch people quickly say 'Zeg maar je' ('Just call me je'), so do not worry if you start with **u**.

summary: Use **ik ben ...**, **ik heet ...** or **mijn naam is ...** to give your name.
Ask **Hoe heet je?** informally and **Hoe heet u?** politely.
Use **ik kom uit ...** for your country.
**Zijn** is irregular: **ik ben, jij bent, hij is**.
Use **je** with peers and **u** with older strangers or officials.
